review.coverage: 204 tests, 200 distinct n spanning 1..1e6 (n=1e6 twice), every n<=10, 175 tests with n>106.
review.crlfIndependence: Every incorrect source was re-run on LF-normalized copies of all test inputs; first failing test unchanged and numerically wrong answers persist, so no counterexample depends on CRLF line endings.
review.incorrectAreAlgorithmic: Every incorrect source read in full; each prints a numerically wrong answer on valid tests (format/debug-only failures not counted).
review.independentOracle: Alternating DP: for marble i add (count ending in the other colour + 1) to the count ending in its colour, mod 1e9+7; cross-checked against enumeration of all subsequences for n<=16.
review.officialTests: official_tests_complete=true, testset_size 50; package tests 0001-0050 equal the pinned row's official tests positionally (CRLF-normalized inputs, token-equal outputs); source row equals the sha-verified pinned parquet row; test bytes unchanged from the previously audited package.
review.oracleResult: All 204 package tests and all samples pass a strict format/range parse; every expected output equals my oracle; all upstream official rows equal my oracle.
review.sandbox: Own harness (sha256 c582ff42...983d0d; 704A re-judged with a token-hash variant because outputs exceed 200 bytes; not worker pool_harness): pinned python@sha256:5887f265...05d3, --network=none, --read-only, --user=65534, --cap-drop=ALL, no-new-privileges, pids<=32, 1 CPU, 2560m memory, RLIMIT_CPU/AS at problem limits, bounded output, launched from env -i shell without credentials; g++ -O2 -std=c++17 -DONLINE_JUDGE.
review.singleAnswer: Output is uniquely determined by the input; token comparison is correct; no special checker or float tolerance.
review.statement: Packaged bound '1 ≤ n ≤ 10<sup>6</sup>'; original package HTML ('≤ 106') preserved byte-identical (equals previously packaged statement) in statement-sources/209A.original.html, one-line diff; attested raw codeforces.me 209/A snapshot hash matches and contains sup.upper-index markup; I re-fetched codeforces.me myself (10<sup>6</sup>). Modulus is written out as 1000000007, so '(109 + 7)' is not ambiguous.
review.submissionProvenance: All sources byte-identical (sha256) to rows in pinned open-r1/codeforces-submissions shards (shard sha256 verified independently); upstream verdict/problem/language match; for every incorrect source the first failing package test equals upstream passedTestCount+1.
